newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police arrest eight in security raids.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police arrest eight in security raids.

text.p: Northern Ireland police arrested eight people on Thursday in a crackdown on suspected IRA guerrilla activity in Belfast, British security sources said.

Several homes were searched in Catholic parts of west Belfast by security forces probing an upswing in hostilities by the outlawed Irish Republican Army (IRA), which is fighting to end British rule in the province, according to the sources.
"A number of people have been arrested in west Belfast this morning in connection with terrorist crime," a police spokesman said.
Security officers say there is a high risk of IRA attacks on soldiers and police across the province during the guerrillas' current offensive.
Late on Wednesday, a police patrol in the town of Dungannon, 40 miles (60 km) west of Belfast, narrowly escaped injury in a suspected IRA bomb attack.
No group claimed responsibility but security sources said it bore the hallmarks of IRA militants, who have launched a spate of mortar and grenade attacks recently.

In Downpatrick town two weeks ago, a parked car exploded when three off-duty soldiers were about to get into it. Last week in Belfast an army patrol had a lucky escape when two grenades were fired at it.
Part of the cross-border Belfast to Dublin rail line was closed on Thursday in a security alert near a station in Lurgan, 30 miles (50 km) south-west of Belfast.
Police said three men were arrested after "suspicious activity" near the railway station. Around 100 homes were evacuated.
Police did not specify what had aroused suspicion but said security forces were searching the area.
British and Irish Republic ministers were due to meet in London on Thursday evening to discuss difficulties plaguing the Northern Ireland peace process.

Irish Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring and Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew were holding their first bi-lateral talks of this year against a background of unresolved political stability and a growing guerrilla threat.
The IRA abandoned a 17-month ceasefire a year ago, blaming Britain for keeping its Sinn Fein political wing out current multiparty of peace talks.
Britain says Sinn Fein will be given a place at the talks if the IRA definitively abandons military action.
But security security sources in Northern Ireland say there is no sign of any move by the IRA to call off its activities.
